newsitem.title: CHINA: China says brisk export pace likely to ease in '97.
newsitem.headline: China says brisk export pace likely to ease in '97.

text.p: China's fast pace of exports recorded over the January-April period is unlikely to be maintained over the full year, the Business Weekly on Sunday quoted economists as saying.

They were quoted as saying that exports would remain healthy though they would fall short of the growth of 26.9 percent registered in the first four months of the year compared with the same period in 1996.

"Although it is impossible to maintain a 20 percent growth rate throughout the year, the year-round rate can maintain double digit growth," said Zhang Xiaoji, a director of the State Council's (cabinet) Development and Research Institute.
The newspaper, published by the official China Daily, also quoted Li Jian, a researcher at the Foreign Trade Institute as saying that the rise in exports would not reach double digits.
China's exports in the January-April period reached $50.26 billion while imports dipped 0.5 percent to $40 billion.
The $10.29 billion trade surplus for the period compared with a $607 million deficit in the same months of 1996.
Chinese economists have said they expected to see exports remain fairly strong for the full year.
The Business Weekly export processing companies as well as foreign funded firms and non-state owned enterprises were likely to drive exports this year.
It warned anti-dumping measures by some of China's major markets could affect the export picture in the months ahead. Some labour-intensive products were seen as vulnerable.
A stable exchange rate for the nation's currency was benefiting exports while tax rebates for exporters were also helping the trade picture.
